title: Terraform module: multi-tenant KMS/HSM key routing + Vault/SecretsManager orchestration for Private VPC
creator: Alicia Park
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that orchestrates KMS/HSM key provisioning and secrets routing for Private (VPC) deployments. The module must support both AWS KMS/CloudHSM and on-prem HSMs (via customer-provided PKCS#11 endpoints), provide Vault and Secrets Manager backends, and offer a clear upgrade path for KMS provider versions and key rotation. The goal is to standardize key aliasing, tenant scoping, and health checks so Platform Ops can reliably deploy Private clusters with minimal manual steps.
background_and_motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private require strict separation of customer keys, auditable key rotation, and automated secrets plumbing. Existing infra work has ad-hoc scripts that differ per cloud and customer; this results in operational overhead during upgrades and incidents. We need a canonical Terraform module to encapsulate best practices, integrate with our Private control plane bootstrap, and surface health metrics to the Console.
design_notes: Module will expose two top-level resources: key_store (abstracts KMS or HSM) and secrets_backend_bindings (Vault path or Secrets Manager ARNs).
Support multi-tenant naming convention: redwood/{customer_id}/{env}/{purpose} with idempotent alias creation to avoid collisions on reapply.

Implement optional PKCS#11 connector block for on-prem HSMs; validate using a provider-agnostic health check that tests signing and encryption roundtrip during apply (non-blocking but failing plan when --check-health flag is used).
Provide versioned providers: recommend pinned provider versions with migration helpers and a terraform state import guide for customers upgrading from older module variants.

Key rotation: module supports scheduled rotation via tagging and an external rotation webhook target; rotation performed in two-stage: create new key -> re-encrypt secrets -> swap alias -> schedule old key for retire.
Telemetry: emit outputs for key ARNs/IDs, alias, and a healthcheck_url for runtime probes. These outputs will be consumed by bootstrap and Console registration.
Security: least-privilege IAM roles for automation user; optional customer-managed KMS grants for cross-account access.
Backends: Vault integration supports AppRole auth and path-level policies; Secrets Manager integration supports replication config for multi-region Private clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module repo created under infra/modules/kms-orchestration with README and examples for AWS KMS + Vault, AWS KMS + Secrets Manager, and On-Prem HSM + Vault.
Module passes unit tests (terratest) that spin up ephemeral AWS account resources in CI (mocked where required) and run healthcheck scenarios.
Upgrade guide documented: step-by-step migration for customers on provider v3.x -> v4.x with sample import commands and rollback plan.
E2E private-bootstrap flow updated to consume module outputs and register key metadata with control plane.
Security review completed and signed off by Security guild; example IAM policies published.
Console displays key health status for deployed Private clusters using new healthcheck_url output.
Performance: module provisioning time for typical customer (single region) under 20 minutes in happy path.
No hard-coded secrets or plaintext keys in repo; CI verifies secrets scanning rules.

Implement AWS KMS + Vault example and local terratest suite
Add PKCS#11 connector and on-prem acceptance test harness
Implement healthcheck lambda/container that performs sign/encrypt roundtrip
Document upgrade and import strategies; add migration helpers (scripts)
Add IAM least-privilege templates and example policies
Add CI job with terratest/parallel mocks and secret scanning
Coordinate rollout with Private bootstrap and Console teams
